control_failures.control_label: availability and testing of fixed fire protection

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: unplanned release of chemical energy at P-4101

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control FIXED_FIRE_SYSTEM_AVAILABILITY: the availability and testing of fixed fire protection had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next assurance activity that the availability and testing of fixed fire protection on P-4101, M-4101 and TT-4101 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in mustering and rescuing, specifically alarming, mustering and accounting for people. P-4101 (hydrocarbon transfer pumps) is in service for hydrocarbon transfer, single mechanical seal with pressurised barrier-fluid support. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the availability and testing of fixed fire protection had degraded below its design intent. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 28 May 2026 a high potential incident was recorded on P-4101, M-4101 and TT-4101 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during a planned shutdown; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
